analysis.title: Coffee Break: US midterms trigger energy reassessment
key_insights: Brent and TTF fell 20% and 15% respectively from their recent highs in the run-up to and aftermath of the US midterm elections, on hopes the new Congress will pressure the administration to resolve the Iran and Ukraine conflicts.
UniCredit says oil and gas prices have been driven more by geopolitical fear in recent months than by supply and demand fundamentals, so the geopolitical premium remains the main price driver.

Republican losses in Congress exceeded the most optimistic Democratic forecasts. The result is read as a rebuke of the Trump administration's foreign policy, especially the decision to go to war with Iran.
A Gallup poll before the election put the 'situation in Iran' and 'gas prices' near the top of voter concerns, ahead of immigration, crime and abortion.

Trump has said further airstrikes on Iran are likely not necessary, and the price drop has continued. UniCredit notes he has shown no sign of easing military pressure and sees this as an ongoing danger, especially toward end-2026 while he still has a loyal lame-duck Congress.

US policy could turn more dovish toward Iran and more hawkish toward Russia in 2027 under the new Democratic Congress. UniCredit adds that the executive branch keeps broad authority over foreign affairs that Congress will struggle to constrain.
Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russian diesel just before they took effect in October was criticised by prominent Democrats and Republicans but had no perceptible impact on US energy prices.
UniCredit sees some potential for energy price relief in the coming months, but expects uncertainty and short-term volatility to stay high.

UniCredit expects October US CPI at +0.3% mom headline and +0.2% mom core. It forecasts yoy headline CPI rising to 4.0% from 3.7% and core to 2.8% from 2.6%, driven by base effects, with petrol prices broadly unchanged in October.

sector_views.rationale: Some potential for oil and gas price relief in coming months as the geopolitical premium unwinds, but near-term volatility stays high because the premium is still the main price driver.

macro_indicators.interpretation: UniCredit forecast, up from 3.7% in the previous reading, due to base effects. No consensus figure is given.
UniCredit forecast, up from 2.6% previously. No consensus figure is given.
UniCredit forecast, matching a consensus of 0.3%, versus 0.6% previously. Petrol prices were broadly unchanged in October, so energy added little.
UniCredit forecast, matching a consensus of 0.2%, versus 0.3% previously.

risk_factors: Trump continues military pressure on Iran, especially toward end-2026 during the lame-duck session with a loyal Congress.
The executive branch's broad authority over international affairs limits how far the new Congress can constrain policy.
Short-term energy price volatility stays high because of the geopolitical premium.
Higher yoy CPI from base effects: headline to 4.0% from 3.7%.
vol_and_positioning: UniCredit expects short-term energy price volatility to stay pronounced because the geopolitical premium is the main price driver.
geopolitical: US-Iran war and the possibility of further US airstrikes on Iran, which Trump has said are likely not necessary
Russia-Ukraine conflict and falling US public support for military aid to Ukraine (57% in July to 44%)
Trump's waiver of sanctions on Russian diesel before the October effective date, despite the 'Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026'
Republican 2028 hopefuls JD Vance and Ron DeSantis distancing themselves from the Iran war decision

tension_points.theme: US energy and foreign policy after midterms
tension_points.bull_case: Republican midterm losses and the new Democratic Congress in 2027 could push the administration toward resolving the Iran and Ukraine conflicts. This would deflate the geopolitical premium, and UniCredit sees potential energy price relief in the coming months.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump has shown no signs of easing military pressure on Iran and keeps a loyal Congress through the lame-duck session. The executive branch has broad authority over international affairs that the new Congress will struggle to constrain.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued or escalated US military pressure on Iran during the lame-duck session toward the end of 2026.

theme_stances.key_argument: Oil and gas prices have been driven more by geopolitical fears than by supply and demand, so the midterm results could allow some relief.
theme_stances.evidence: geopolitical premium remains the main price driver
